$comment: Literal, reusable prompt blocks for NuLumin hero scenes on Nano Banana Pro. These are the surviving text after many rejected rounds — edit them only with a reason. Placeholders: {name} {dose} {rules} {cap} {cake}. See HERO_PROMPTS.md for the technique.

references.$comment: Reference ORDER is load-bearing. The label crop is the single fix that stopped label drift — given only a small whole vial, the model re-letters the label from comprehension.

2.what: a HIGH-RESOLUTION CLOSE-UP CROP OF THE LABEL — the authority on typography

blocks.product:
THE PRODUCT — reproduce the vial from the reference image EXACTLY:
· REFERENCE IMAGE 1 is the whole vial. REFERENCE IMAGE 2 is a HIGH-RESOLUTION CLOSE-UP OF THE LABEL — copy the label from THAT image, letterform for letterform. It is the authority on the typography.
· Clear glass NuLumin vial. COPY the label pixel-for-pixel. Do not re-letter, re-typeset, re-space, restyle, translate or invent anything on it. Every glyph, weight, size and position must match the reference. For certainty, the label reads, top to bottom, with TWO clearly visible {rules} vertical rules running the full height of its LEFT edge — a thicker one hard on the label's left border and a second thinner one set slightly inboard of it. These rules must be present and obvious; do not omit, fade or grey them out. Reading top to bottom:
    "NuLumin"  — "Nu" in heavy weight, "Lumin" in light weight, one word, in BLACK
    a thin full-width horizontal rule beneath it
    "BIO-SCIENCES" — small, widely letter-spaced BLACK capitals
    "{name}" — large ITALIC SERIF in a HIGH-CONTRAST DIDONE style (think Bodoni or Didot italic): dramatic thick-to-thin stroke modulation, very fine hairline strokes and crisp flat hairline serifs, elegant and calligraphic. Set in a REGULAR / BOOK weight. This is critical: it is NOT bold, NOT black, NOT heavy. It is an elegant light-to-medium serif with fine hairline strokes and delicate thin-to-thick contrast, like classical book typography. Do not thicken, embolden or fatten these letterforms. It is BLACK — only the dose is coloured.
    "{dose}" — large serif in the SAME COLOUR as the two vertical rules, also REGULAR weight, not bold
    "Manufactured by NuLumin" — small monospaced type
  and a small thin-ruled box in the upper RIGHT corner containing three tiny lines of fine print.
  The label is smooth premium coated stock, flat against the glass, no curl, no distortion.
· FILL LEVEL IS EXACT: the powder occupies ONLY THE BOTTOM THIRD of the vial. The upper two-thirds of the vial is EMPTY — clear, transparent, air-filled glass you can see straight through. The vial is NOT full, NOT filled to the shoulder, NOT filled to the neck. · THE VIAL MUST CONTAIN PRODUCT: that bottom third holds {cake}, clearly visible through the glass. The vial must never look empty.
· THE CAKE MUST LOOK LIKE A REAL LYOPHILIZED PHARMACEUTICAL CAKE — THIS IS NOT LOOSE POWDER:
  It is a SOLID, COHESIVE, FREEZE-DRIED PLUG that holds its own shape. It spans the FULL internal width of the vial and sits as one intact disc with a FLAT, LEVEL, slightly matte top surface and a clean, sharply defined horizontal edge where it meets the glass. Its texture is a dense micro-porous solid — like a firm compressed tablet or a set block of chalk — not granular, not loose, not heaped, not poured.
  ABSOLUTELY NOT: loose powder, flour, sugar, sand, granules, a heaped or mounded pile, a sloped or uneven surface, visible individual particles, cracks, fissures, chunks or a collapsed centre. If it looks like something poured from a bag, it is WRONG.
· MATERIAL: flagship luxury-cosmetics product photography. Brilliant wet-look glossy glass, liquid-sharp specular highlights, a long crisp vertical highlight down one side, true refraction and visible glass thickness at the shoulder and base, and a polished mirror-finish aluminium crimp collar with sharp metallic reflections. THE FLIP CAP IS COLOURED: {cap}, seated on a polished silver aluminium crimp collar beneath it. Coloured cap on top, silver crimp ring below it, in that order.
· LIGHT THE LABEL FROM THE FRONT: a soft, even frontal key light falls directly on the label so every line is evenly exposed and fully legible. Do NOT backlight or rim-light the vial in a way that silhouettes it, throws the label into shadow, or blows it out with glow.
· THE LABEL IS SACRED: nothing may cross, veil or overlap it. No flare, no vapour, no element in front of it. It faces the camera almost straight on, rotated 6-9 degrees, pin-sharp, high contrast, the crispest thing in frame. The ENTIRE vial including its full label and base sits inside the frame, never cropped.
· SEPARATION IS THE TOP PRIORITY — ALL ATTENTION ON THE VIAL:
  · EXTREME shallow depth of field, shot wide open at roughly f/1.4 on a macro lens. ONLY the vial's label plane is in focus. Everything else — the vapour, the surface, the frost, the far background — melts into a heavy, creamy, strongly defocused blur with soft round bokeh. The blur should be dramatic and obvious, not subtle, and it should begin immediately behind the vial.
  · HIGH CONTRAST: the background sits several stops DARKER than the vial — deep, near-black shadow falling off fast toward the frame edges. The vial is lit like a jewel in a spotlight: a bright, clean pool of light on it alone, with a crisp brilliant rim of light tracing both of its edges to lift it off the dark ground. Strong vignette.
  · Any vapour, glow or effect around the vial stays LOW, soft and out of focus, and must never brighten to compete with the product or rise across the label.
  · The vial and its label are unmistakably the sharpest, brightest, highest-contrast thing in the picture by a wide margin. The eye should have nowhere else to go.
Ultra-high-resolution. Photoreal. No added text, words, logos or watermarks anywhere.
blocks.empty:
THERE IS NO PRODUCT IN THIS IMAGE. It is an EMPTY SET — a bare stage photographed before the product was placed on it. Absolutely nothing stands on the surface: no bottle, no vial, no jar, no box, no object of any kind, and no text, logos or watermarks. Just the empty environment.
THE SURFACE DESCRIBED ABOVE runs as a horizontal plane across the LOWER PORTION of the frame, its far horizon fading into darkness. Above it is a VAST, EMPTY, DEEP dark void — smooth dark gradient, nothing in it at all.
Shot on a macro lens at roughly f/1.4 from a low camera height, so the surface plane is seen almost edge-on and everything falls away into a heavy creamy defocus. There is a clean, bright POOL OF LIGHT on the empty surface in the centre of the lower half where a product would be placed, falling off fast into deep near-black shadow at the frame edges. Strong vignette. Ultra-high-resolution, photoreal.

composition.$comment: Both ratios use the SAME structural wording on purpose. Percentage-only briefs get ignored — a briefed 'upper 42% empty' rendered as 34%. The horizontal-centre-line rule is the one instruction that has actually held. Giving 4:5 its own description is what made the two placements diverge.
composition.9:16: COMPOSITION IS EXACT AND THE VIAL MUST BE BIG: THE ENTIRE UPPER HALF OF THE IMAGE IS EMPTY DARK SPACE. The vial's cap does NOT begin until BELOW THE VERTICAL MIDPOINT of the frame — if you drew a horizontal line across the exact centre of the image, the whole vial including its cap sits BENEATH that line. Nothing but empty dark gradient above it. The cap's top edge is about 55% down from the top. Below that the vial is the LARGE, DOMINANT hero of the frame — it spans roughly 46% of the total frame width. Its BASE must also sit clearly ABOVE the bottom edge of the frame with a clear margin of empty surface beneath it — the whole vial floats in the middle-lower band of the picture, touching neither the midpoint above nor the bottom edge below. It is a close, imposing product shot, not a small object in a big room. Standing upright and CENTRED horizontally in the frame — the dead-centre focal point of the image.
composition.4:5: COMPOSITION IS EXACT: THE ENTIRE UPPER HALF OF THE IMAGE IS EMPTY DARK SPACE. The vial's cap does NOT begin until BELOW THE VERTICAL MIDPOINT of the frame — if you drew a horizontal line across the exact centre of the image, the whole vial including its cap sits BENEATH that line. Nothing but empty dark gradient above it. The cap's top edge is about 52% down from the top. Below that the vial stands upright and CENTRED horizontally, spanning roughly 30% of the total frame width. Its BASE must also sit clearly ABOVE the bottom edge of the frame with a clear margin of empty surface beneath it — the whole vial floats in the lower half of the picture, touching neither the midpoint above nor the bottom edge below. The whole vial, cap to base, is complete and fully visible — never cropped.

cryo.prompt: A deep, dark violet-black cold chamber. Dense CRYOGENIC VAPOUR — heavy freeze-dry fog — rolls and pours slowly around the base of the vial and spills forward across the surface, catching a hard rim of violet light. Wisps curl upward but NEVER cross the label. A single cold, hard key light rakes from the upper left, carving the vapour into volumetric shafts. Frost crystals glitter faintly on the surface beneath. Cinematic, frozen, laboratory-sublime. Deep shadow, brilliant specular edges.
cryo.why: Lyophilisation made visible — dramatic, and tied to what the product actually is.

caustics.prompt: A sculptural monolithic surface of polished dark violet stone under a single hard light. Brilliant liquid CAUSTIC light patterns — the rippling refracted light you get through thick glass and water — dance across the stone surface and up the back wall in sharp bright violet-white filigree. The vial stands on the stone, casting a long crisp shadow and throwing its own caustic pool of light. Museum-lit, high contrast, expensive, tactile. Deep blacks, saturated violet, brilliant white caustics.
caustics.why: Luxury-cosmetics language: light bent through glass. Sculptural and rich.

causticsblue.prompt:
A sculptural monolithic surface of polished dark INDIGO-BLUE stone under a single hard light. Brilliant liquid CAUSTIC light patterns — the rippling refracted light you get through thick glass and water — dance across the stone surface and up the back wall in sharp bright CYAN-WHITE filigree. Museum-lit, high contrast, expensive, tactile. Deep blacks, saturated indigo blue, brilliant cyan-white caustics. NO fog, NO vapour, NO smoke, NO frost and NO ice anywhere in the image.
The stone runs EDGE TO EDGE across the bottom of the frame as one solid continuous floor that continues past the left and right frame borders. It is NEVER a floating slab, platform, plinth, podium, pedestal or table, and none of its side, front or corner edges are ever visible — showing them makes the image read as a cheap 3D render.
The BRIGHTEST caustics play on the BACK WALL and toward the OUTER edges of the floor. The centre of the floor, where a product would stand, stays comparatively DARK, calm and evenly lit — a soft pool, never a blown-out white hotspot.
causticsblue.why: The panel gets the surviving non-cryo style, tinted to the cellular spectrum band. Creative #1 owns cryo; rebuilding the panel in the same fog is what got it rejected as too similar.

plate.prompt: A completely plain, empty, seamless DEEP VIOLET-BLACK studio background — a smooth unbroken gradient with NO surface texture, NO table, NO horizon line, NO props, NO fog, NO frost, NO particles and NO pattern of any kind. The vial floats against this plain ground. A single hard key light from the upper left with a bright crisp rim of light tracing BOTH vertical edges of the glass to separate it from the ground, and a soft frontal fill on the label. The background falls away to near-black at every frame edge.
plate.why: A CUTTING PLATE. One vial on a plain seamless so it can be matted out and placed into a set by hand. This is how multi-vial creatives get correct labels: rendering three vials in one shot re-letters all three, whereas one vial per generation is the exact condition under which the label has always held.

dropped.chromatogram: Glowing spectral peaks. Rejected twice — the vial and label read badly against the luminous curves no matter how the lighting was constrained.
dropped.inkbloom: Pigment in water. Beautiful, but the bloom climbs into the text zone and reads like a fragrance ad.
dropped.powderburst: Suspended powder. Rejected on the same grounds.
dropped.lightstreak: The earlier per-SKU hero style. Still approved for standalone SKU marketing, but the client called it generic underneath ad copy.
